preamble: This design describes the technical shape of shopapi, a FastAPI service for customer registration, tier promotion, and order lifecycle management backed by PostgreSQL, Redis, and an external courier rates API (from python).

Bootstrap loads Settings from the environment and `.env`, wires shared Cache and orders ShippingClient, and exposes versioned REST routers for customers and orders plus unversioned health endpoints, with domain exceptions mapped to HTTP responses (from python).

blocks.text: Shopapi is a FastAPI application titled shopapi at version 1.2.0 whose lifespan configures logging from settings, connects Redis for shared caching, logs readiness on the listen port, and on shutdown closes the shipping HTTP client and the cache connection (REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-006, REQ-007, REQ-008, REQ-010). Configuration is centralized in Settings with prefix SHOPAPI_ and defaults for port, database, Redis, shipping API URL, timeouts, pagination, CORS origins, and API bearer tokens (REQ-001, REQ-002).

HTTP surface area splits into GET /health and GET /health/ready without an API version prefix (REQ-017), and customers plus orders routers mounted under /api/v1 at /customers and /orders respectively (REQ-018, REQ-020). Customers and orders routes expect bearer authentication against settings.api_tokens (REQ-019, REQ-021, REQ-023). Orders integrate catalogue pricing, tier and bulk discounts, zone-based shipping quotes with retries, and state transitions; customers support registration, cached reads, and monotonic tier promotion (REQ-024, REQ-032, REQ-038, REQ-053, REQ-058).

Runtime configuration and shared infrastructure types anchor the stack: Settings drives env-backed defaults; Cache abstracts Redis get/set/invalidate; ShippingClient wraps httpx calls to the external rates service (from python).

type.signature:
class Settings(BaseSettings):
    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_prefix="SHOPAPI_", env_file=".env")
    port: int = 8000
    database_url: str = "postgresql+psycopg://shop:shop@localhost:5432/shop"
    redis_url: str = "redis://localhost:6379/0"
    shipping_api_url: str = "https://rates.courier.example/v2"
    shipping_api_key: str = ""
    request_timeout_s: float = 5.0
    cache_ttl_s: int = 300
    order_cache_ttl_s: int = 60
    default_page_size: int = 20
    max_page_size: int = 100
    api_tokens: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    cors_origins: list[str] = Field(default_factory=lambda: ["http://localhost:3000"])
    log_level: str = "info"

class Cache:
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...
    async def connect(self) -> None: ...
    async def close(self) -> None: ...
    async def get(self, key: str) -> Any | None: ...
    async def set(self, key: str, value: Any, ttl_s: int | None = None) -> None: ...
    async def invalidate(self, *keys: str) -> None: ...

class ShippingClient:
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...
    async def close(self) -> None: ...
    async def quote(self, postcode: str, weight_grams: int) -> dict: ...
    async def _get_with_retry(self, path: str, params: dict) -> dict: ...

blocks.text: Domain errors NotFoundError, ConflictError, ValidationError, and UpstreamError propagate from services and are translated at the HTTP boundary (REQ-013, REQ-014, REQ-015, REQ-016).

type.signature:
class NotFoundError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, kind: str, id: str | int) -> None: ...

class ConflictError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, state: str, message: str) -> None: ...

class ValidationError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, field: str, message: str) -> None: ...

class UpstreamError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, system: str, message: str) -> None: ...

blocks.text: Customers are identified by string UUIDs with unique lowercased email, name, tier, and timestamps; API bodies use CustomerIn and CustomerOut while persistence uses SQLAlchemy Customer on Base (REQ-025, REQ-031).

type.signature: Tier = Literal["standard", "silver", "gold"]

class CustomerIn(BaseModel):
    email: EmailStr
    name: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=120)
    tier: Tier = "standard"

class CustomerOut(BaseModel):
    id: str
    email: str
    name: str
    tier: Tier
    created_at: str

class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    ...

class Customer(Base):
    __tablename__ = "customers"
    id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(36), primary_key=True)
    email: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(254), unique=True, index=True)
    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(120))
    tier: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(16), default="standard")
    created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(DateTime)

class CustomerRepository:
    def __init__(self, db: Session) -> None: ...
    def find(self, customer_id: str) -> Customer | None: ...
    def by_email(self, email: str) -> Customer | None: ...
    def insert(self, customer: Customer) -> Customer: ...

class CustomerService:
    def __init__(self, repository: CustomerRepository) -> None: ...
    async def get(self, customer_id: str) -> Customer: ...
    def register(self, request: CustomerIn) -> Customer: ...
    async def promote(self, customer_id: str, tier: str) -> Customer: ...

blocks.text: Orders aggregate priced lines, ship-to address JSON, monetary fields, and a transitions history; catalogue Product rows supply unit price, weight, and stock for placement and amendments (REQ-057, REQ-075).

type.signature:
class DeliveryZone:
    start: str
    end: str
    zone: str
    courier: str
    min_days: int
    rural: bool
OrderState = Literal["pending", "paid", "packed", "shipped", "delivered", "cancelled"]

class Address(BaseModel):
    name: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=120)
    line1: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=120)
    line2: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=120)
    city: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=80)
    postcode: str = Field(pattern=r"^\d{4}$")

class PlaceOrder(BaseModel):
    customer_id: str
    lines: list[LineIn] = Field(min_length=1, max_length=MAX_LINES)
    ship_to: Address
    courier_note: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=280)
    def skus_unique(cls, lines: list[LineIn]) -> list[LineIn]: ...

class AmendLines(BaseModel):
    lines: list[LineIn] = Field(min_length=1, max_length=MAX_LINES)

class Line(Base):
    __tablename__ = "order_lines"
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True, autoincrement=True)
    order_id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(ForeignKey("orders.id"), index=True)
    sku: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(32))
    quantity: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer)
    unit_cents: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer)
    weight_grams: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer)
    order: Mapped[Order] = relationship(back_populates="lines")

class LineOut(BaseModel):
    sku: str
    quantity: int
    unit_cents: int
    weight_grams: int

class Order(Base):
    __tablename__ = "orders"
    id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(36), primary_key=True)
    customer_id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(ForeignKey("customers.id"), index=True)
    state: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(16), default="pending", index=True)
    ship_to: Mapped[dict] = mapped_column(JSON)
    courier_note: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(280), nullable=True)
    subtotal_cents: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer)
    discount_cents: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer, default=0)
    shipping_cents: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer)
    total_cents: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer)
    transitions: Mapped[list] = mapped_column(JSON, default=list)
    created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(DateTime)
    updated_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(DateTime)
    lines: Mapped[list["Line"]] = relationship(back_populates="order", cascade="all, delete-orphan")

class OrderOut(BaseModel):
    id: str
    customer_id: str
    state: OrderState
    lines: list[LineOut]
    ship_to: Address
    courier_note: str | None
    subtotal_cents: int
    discount_cents: int
    shipping_cents: int
    total_cents: int
    created_at: str
    updated_at: str

class Page(BaseModel):
    items: list[OrderOut]
    total: int
    page: int
    size: int

class Product(Base):
    __tablename__ = "products"
    sku: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(32), primary_key=True)
    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(120))
    unit_cents: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer)
    weight_grams: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer)
    stock: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer, default=0)

class Priced:
    sku: str
    quantity: int
    unit_cents: int
    weight_grams: int

class OrderRepository:
    def __init__(self, db: Session) -> None: ...
    def find(self, order_id: str) -> Order | None: ...
    def list(self, *, customer_id: str | None, state: str | None, page: int, size: int) -> tuple[list[Order], int]: ...
    def insert(self, order: Order) -> Order: ...
    def update(self, order: Order) -> Order: ...

class OrderService:
    def __init__(self, repository: OrderRepository, catalogue: Catalogue, customers: CustomerService, shipping: ShippingClient) -> None: ...
    async def get(self, order_id: str) -> Order: ...
    def list(self, *, customer_id: str | None, state: str | None, page: int, size: int) -> tuple[list[Order], int]: ...
    async def place(self, request: PlaceOrder) -> Order: ...
    async def amend(self, order_id: str, request: AmendLines) -> Order: ...
    async def transition(self, order_id: str, state: str, reason: str | None) -> Order: ...
    def price(self, lines: list[LineIn]) -> list[Priced]: ...

blocks.text: At startup the shared cache connects via Redis.from_url(settings.redis_url, decode_responses=True) and pings the server before the app accepts traffic (REQ-005, from python).
Shutdown closes the orders module ShippingClient httpx AsyncClient with aclose and tears down the Redis client when open (from python).

Shipping quotes use GET against settings.shipping_api_url (default https://rates.courier.example/v2) with query zone and weight, Authorization Bearer settings.shipping_api_key, and timeout settings.request_timeout_s; place order and amend lines share the same retry policy on transport errors and 5xx (REQ-065, REQ-076, from python).

Customer registration detects duplicate email with a SQLAlchemy select filtered on the lowercased address; successful handlers commit the ORM session and failures roll back on the customers routes (REQ-042, REQ-043, from python).

Customer get uses json.loads on Redis payloads for key customer:{customer_id} and json.dumps with TTL settings.cache_ttl_s on store; order get uses order:{order_id} with settings.order_cache_ttl_s (REQ-035, REQ-071, from python).

Order list queries orders with lines eager-loaded, optional customer_id and state filters, created_at descending, offset/limit pagination, and a count over the filtered subquery (REQ-055, from python). Order fetch by id selects the order with lines selectinloaded; product rows load by sku set during placement (from python).

Liveness probes the database with select 1 on engine.connect() via sqlalchemy text; cache liveness uses ping when a client exists (REQ-047, REQ-050, from python). Readiness returns ready true without dependency checks (REQ-052, from python).

Structured logging emits info when shopapi is ready on settings.port, when a customer registers with id and tier, when an order is placed with ids and total_cents, and error on upstream failures for UpstreamError (REQ-006, REQ-030, from python).
Lifespan runs logging.basicConfig from settings.log_level, awaits cache.connect(), logs readiness on settings.port, then on shutdown awaits orders.shipping.close() and cache.close() (from python).

CORSMiddleware allows settings.cors_origins with methods GET, POST, and PUT and headers authorization and content-type; HTTP timing middleware adds a server-timing header with app duration in milliseconds; four domain exception handlers cover NotFound, Conflict, Validation, and Upstream; health mounts without a version prefix while orders and customers mount under /api/v1 (REQ-011, REQ-012, REQ-013, REQ-014, REQ-015, REQ-016, from python).

The customers APIRouter mounts at prefix /customers with tag customers and router-level dependency Authed so bearer validation runs before register, get_customer, and promote (from python). Register lowercases email, rejects an existing row via by_email with ConflictError state registered, builds a Customer with uuid4 id and UTC created_at, inserts it, logs customer id and tier at info, and returns the persisted entity (REQ-026, REQ-027, REQ-028, REQ-029, from python).

Get reads customer:{id} from cache; on hit reconstructs Customer from JSON; on miss loads by primary key, raises NotFoundError when absent, otherwise sets cache with a dumped dict and settings.cache_ttl_s; when Cache.client is None, get behaves as a miss (REQ-033, REQ-034, REQ-036, REQ-037, from python).

Promote validates tier membership in TIERS (standard, silver, gold), loads the customer via get, refuses non-increasing tier rank with ConflictError, updates tier, re-inserts the row, and deletes the customer cache key (REQ-039, REQ-040, REQ-041, from python).

GET /health runs synchronous database check and await cache check, sets status_code 503 if any check is false, and returns status ok or degraded with a checks map for database and cache booleans (REQ-044, REQ-045, REQ-046, from python). GET /health/ready responds with ready true unconditionally (from python).

The orders APIRouter mounts at prefix /orders with tags orders and applies the Authed dependency to every route (from python). Place order assigns a UUID, copies ship_to and courier_note, seeds transitions with pending at placement time, builds Line rows from priced catalogue lines, and logs order id, customer id, and total_cents; shipping uses ShippingClient with httpx against settings.shipping_api_url, timeout, and Bearer key (from python).

ShippingClient resolves postcode to a zone, fetches rates, selects lowest price_cents, applies tier and bulk discount logic, waives shipping at threshold, adds RURAL_SURCHARGE_CENTS for rural zones when free shipping does not apply, and sets total_cents from subtotal minus discount plus shipping (REQ-063, REQ-066, REQ-067, REQ-068, REQ-069, from python). Amend lines reprices, requotes with the same retry rules, replaces lines and totals, updates the order, and invalidates order cache for pending orders only (REQ-073, REQ-074, from python). Transition rejects terminal states and invalid targets, requires reason for cancel, appends transition records, persists, and invalidates cache (REQ-077, REQ-078, REQ-079, REQ-080, from python).
Application log level comes from settings.log_level defaulting to info and is applied before serving via lifespan logging configuration (REQ-003, from python).

Registration and order placement emit info logs with entity identifiers and commercial fields; UpstreamError handling logs an upstream failure at error before returning 502 (REQ-016, REQ-030, from python).
Every HTTP response includes a Server-Timing header reporting application duration in milliseconds for request-level latency visibility (REQ-012, from python).
